chunks.title: Solix Enterprise Edition
chunks.text:
Solix Enterprise Edition (Platform). Put AI in the hands of your business.
Enterprise Edition activates your data across every system and every era, so the people who know your business can build the solutions they need, inside the trust perimeter IT defines.
Key capabilities:
- Every system, every era: Connect live ERP, CRM and SaaS alongside retired applications, mainframe extracts and file shares.
- Trust perimeter: Policy-driven access, masking and lineage so business builders never step outside governance.
- Builder workspace: Low-code agents, copilots and dashboards on curated, semantic data products.
- Unified metadata: One catalog across archive, lake and operational sources with automated classification.
- Any deployment: SOLIXCloud, your cloud, on-premises or hybrid, with the same controls everywhere.
- Outcome telemetry: Track adoption, cost savings and compliance posture from a single console.
How it works:
- Connect: Ingest from 150+ connectors and any file format with schema evolution handled for you.
- Govern: Classify, retain, mask and audit automatically against policy templates.
- Activate: Publish trusted data products to analysts, agents and applications.
Typical outcomes:
- 10x faster time to first AI use case
- 1 governed platform instead of six point tools
- 0 copies of sensitive data outside policy

chunks.title: Common Data Platform
chunks.text:
Common Data Platform (Enterprise Foundation). Enterprise data management. Migration. Preservation.
The enterprise-scale data platform that connects to 150+ applications, ingests structured and unstructured data, and provides the governed Preservation Zone that powers every Solix solution. Deployable today.
Key capabilities:
- 150+ connectors: SAP, Oracle, PeopleSoft, Salesforce, Workday, ServiceNow, mainframe, email and files.
- Preservation Zone: Immutable, WORM-capable storage with retention, legal hold and defensible deletion.
- Open formats: Parquet, Iceberg and JSON so your data is never locked in.
- Metadata & catalog: Business glossary, lineage and automated PII discovery.
- Elastic compute: Scale ingest and query independently in any cloud.
- Security by design: Encryption at rest and in transit, RBAC/ABAC, SSO, full audit.
How it works:
- Land: Bulk and incremental ingest with validation and reconciliation reports.
- Organize: Zones for raw, curated, preserved and published data.
- Serve: SQL, REST, search and vector interfaces for every consumer.
Typical outcomes:
- PB scale, proven in production
- 150+ application connectors
- 3 deployment models, one control plane

chunks.title: Enterprise Archiving
chunks.text:
Enterprise Archiving (Cloud Archive Products). Move inactive data out of production. Keep it one click away.
Tier inactive records from ERP, CRM, databases and files to a low-cost, compliant archive with full-text search, retention policies and legal hold, while production gets faster and cheaper.
Key capabilities:
- Policy-based tiering: Business rules decide what moves, when and where.
- Transparent access: Users query archived data from familiar screens and reports.
- Compliance ready: SEC 17a-4, HIPAA, GDPR retention and hold templates.
- Any source: Databases, applications, email, documents, logs.
- Cost intelligence: Chargeback and savings dashboards per application.
- Search everything: Elastic full-text and structured search across the archive.
How it works:
- Assess: Profile growth, access patterns and regulatory retention.
- Archive: Move eligible data with validation and referential integrity.
- Retire: Defensibly delete at end of life with full audit trail.
Typical outcomes:
- 80% lower infrastructure cost
- 3x faster batch and reporting cycles
- 100% audit-ready retention

chunks.title: Enterprise Data Lake
chunks.text:
Enterprise Data Lake (Enterprise Foundation). A governed lake your analysts and models actually trust.
Consolidate structured, semi-structured and unstructured data into an open, catalogued lake with self-service access, quality controls and lineage, ready for BI, data science and AI.
Key capabilities:
- Open table formats: Iceberg and Parquet with time travel and schema evolution.
- Data quality: Rules, anomaly detection and scorecards per dataset.
- Self-service: Marketplace of certified data products with request workflows.
- Lineage: Column-level lineage from source to dashboard to model.
- Vector ready: Embeddings and semantic search for RAG use cases.
- Fine-grained security: Row, column and attribute-based access control.
How it works:
- Ingest: Streaming and batch pipelines with CDC.
- Curate: Transform, certify and publish governed products.
- Analyze: Connect any BI, notebook or AI framework.
Typical outcomes:
- 60% less time finding data
- 1 catalog for lake, archive and apps
- ∞ consumers, zero copies

chunks.title: Application Retirement
chunks.text:
Application Retirement (Cloud Archive Products). Switch off legacy applications. Never lose the data.
Decommission redundant, obsolete and legacy applications while preserving data with full business context for reporting, compliance and eDiscovery. Eliminate licenses, hardware and specialist skills.
Key capabilities:
- Any application: SAP ECC, Oracle EBS, PeopleSoft, JDE, Lotus Notes, mainframe, custom.
- Context preserved: Retain relationships, attachments and business views.
- Report continuity: Pre-built and custom reports on retired data.
- Factory approach: Templates and automation to retire portfolios, not one-offs.
- Chain of custody: Validation, reconciliation and certified extracts.
- Retention by record: Apply granular retention and hold to retired data.
How it works:
- Inventory: Rationalize the portfolio, prioritize by cost and risk.
- Extract: Move data and metadata to the Preservation Zone.
- Decommission: Shut down, cancel licenses, reclaim budget.
Typical outcomes:
- $M annual license and hardware savings
- 90% faster than manual decommissioning
- 0 compliance gaps

chunks.title: eDiscovery
chunks.text:
eDiscovery (Cloud Archive Products). Find, hold and produce records in hours, not weeks.
Search across archived and live data, place legal holds, cull and review, and produce defensible records for litigation, audits and investigations, all on the same governed platform.
Key capabilities:
- Unified search: Email, documents, structured records and chat in one query.
- Legal hold: Custodian-based holds with notifications and audit.
- Early case assessment: Cull by date, custodian, keywords and concepts.
- Review & tag: Collaborative review with privilege and redaction.
- Production: Export to standard load files and formats.
- Defensibility: Immutable audit trail for every action.
How it works:
- Identify: Locate relevant data across every source.
- Preserve: Apply holds instantly, across systems.
- Produce: Review and export with a full chain of custody.
Typical outcomes:
- 70% lower outside review cost
- hrs from request to hold
- 1 source of truth for legal and IT

chunks.title: Consumer Data Privacy
chunks.text:
Consumer Data Privacy (Enterprise Foundation). Know where personal data lives. Prove you handle it right.
Discover and classify personal data across the enterprise, automate DSAR and right-to-be-forgotten requests, enforce consent and retention, and demonstrate compliance with GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA and more.
Key capabilities:
- PII discovery: ML classification across structured and unstructured data.
- DSAR automation: Intake, verification, fulfilment and reporting workflows.
- Right to be forgotten: Orchestrated deletion with legal exceptions.
- Consent management: Capture and enforce purpose-based consent.
- Retention enforcement: Policy-driven minimization across sources.
- Regulator-ready reports: Evidence packs for audits and assessments.
How it works:
- Discover: Map personal data and processing activities.
- Automate: Turn regulations into executable policies.
- Prove: Continuous evidence for every jurisdiction.
Typical outcomes:
- 95% DSARs fulfilled without manual effort
- 30+ regulations covered by templates
- 1 privacy view across the enterprise

chunks.title: Enterprise AI
chunks.text:
Enterprise AI (Enterprise AI (EAI)). Agents and copilots on data you already trust.
Build governed retrieval, agents and AI-ready pipelines on the Common Data Platform. Business users create copilots on curated data products while IT keeps policy, lineage and cost under control.
Key capabilities:
- Governed RAG: Retrieval respects access policy, masking and retention.
- Agent studio: Compose tools, prompts and guardrails without code.
- Model choice: Bring OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini or private models.
- Evaluation: Test sets, grounding scores and drift monitoring.
- Cost control: Budgets, quotas and per-team attribution.
- Audit every answer: Trace each response to its sources.
How it works:
- Curate: Publish AI-ready data products with semantic context.
- Build: Assemble agents and copilots in the studio.
- Operate: Monitor quality, cost and compliance in production.
Typical outcomes:
- weeks not quarters, to production AI
- 100% answers traceable to source
- 0 shadow data copies

chunks.title: Data Sense
chunks.text:
Data Sense (Enterprise AI (EAI)). Know what you have before you build on it.
Automatically classify, profile and map data across every connected system, so every downstream AI product starts from an accurate, current picture of the estate instead of a stale inventory.
Key capabilities:
- Automated classification: ML models tag sensitivity, domain and quality on ingest.
- Living data map: A catalog that updates as systems and schemas change.
- Cross-system profiling: See the same entity across SAP, Salesforce, files and archive.
- Feeds every EAI product: Data Ask, AI Warehouse and Agentic all start from Data Sense.
How it works:
- Connect: Point Data Sense at any connected source.
- Classify: Profile, tag and score data quality automatically.
- Publish: Make the map available to every downstream product.
Typical outcomes:
- 90% less manual data mapping
- 1 living catalog, not a point-in-time audit
- days not quarters, to a governed inventory

chunks.title: Data Ask
chunks.text:
Data Ask (Enterprise AI (EAI)). Ask your enterprise data a question. Get a governed answer.
A natural-language interface over the Common Data Platform, so business teams get direct, policy-checked answers from live, archived and lake data without waiting on a report or a query.
Key capabilities:
- Natural language, real data: Ask in plain English, get answers grounded in governed sources.
- Access-aware: Every answer respects the asker's existing permissions.
- Cites its sources: Every response links back to the records behind it.
- Works across eras: Live, archived and lake data answer the same question.
How it works:
- Ask: Type a question in plain language.
- Retrieve: Data Ask queries governed sources under the asker's access.
- Answer: Get a traceable answer, not a black box.
Typical outcomes:
- mins not days, from question to answer
- 100% answers traceable to source
- 0 new report backlog created

chunks.title: Pre-Build Application Knowledge Graph
chunks.text:
Pre-Build Application Knowledge Graph (Enterprise AI (EAI)). A ready-made semantic map of the systems you already run.
Packaged knowledge graphs for SAP, Oracle and other major applications, encoding entities, relationships and business logic so AI agents understand your systems on day one instead of after months of modeling.
Key capabilities:
- Pre-built for major ERPs: SAP, Oracle EBS and PeopleSoft graphs out of the box.
- Business logic included: Not just tables and columns, but what they mean.
- Extensible: Layer on your own entities and custom objects.
- Built by our AKG team: Or construct your own with AKG Construction Services.
How it works:
- Select: Choose the packaged graph for your core applications.
- Extend: Add custom objects and organization-specific relationships.
- Activate: Agents and copilots reason over the graph immediately.
Typical outcomes:
- weeks not quarters, to a usable knowledge graph
- 1 shared semantic model across AI products
- 0 manual entity mapping to start

chunks.title: AI Warehouse
chunks.text:
AI Warehouse (Enterprise AI (EAI)). Storage built for retrieval, not just reporting.
A governed, AI-ready storage layer with embeddings, vector search and semantic indexing built in, so agents and copilots retrieve the right context without a separate vector database to secure and maintain.
Key capabilities:
- Vector-native: Embeddings and semantic search alongside structured data.
- One governance model: The same access and masking policy as the rest of the platform.
- Model-agnostic: Works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini or private embeddings.
- Elastic scale: Grows with corpus size without a re-architecture.
How it works:
- Index: Embed governed data products automatically.
- Retrieve: Agents query by meaning, not just keyword.
- Refresh: Embeddings stay current as source data changes.
Typical outcomes:
- 1 governed store instead of a shadow vector DB
- 0 sensitive data copied outside policy
- PB scale, same as the rest of the platform

chunks.title: Agentic
chunks.text:
Agentic (Enterprise AI (EAI)). Multi-step agents that act on your data, inside policy.
Compose agents that plan, call tools and take multi-step actions across governed data products, with every action logged, policy-checked and reversible before it touches production.
Key capabilities:
- Tool composition: Chain retrieval, analysis and write-back tools visually.
- Guardrails by default: Every action checked against policy before it runs.
- Human in the loop: Approval steps for anything above a defined risk threshold.
- Full run history: Replay any agent run for audit or debugging.
How it works:
- Compose: Assemble an agent from governed tools and data products.
- Guard: Set approval thresholds and policy checks.
- Operate: Run in production with full observability.
Typical outcomes:
- 100% agent actions logged and auditable
- weeks not quarters, to a production agent
- 0 unreviewed writes to production systems

chunks.title: AI Governance
chunks.text:
AI Governance (Enterprise AI (EAI)). The policy layer every model call runs through.
Centralized policy, lineage and audit for every prompt, retrieval and model response across the enterprise, so risk, legal and IT can see and control AI usage without slowing builders down.
Key capabilities:
- Prompt and response logging: Every interaction retained and searchable for audit.
- Policy enforcement: Access, masking and retention rules apply at inference time.
- Model inventory: Know which models touch which data, everywhere.
- Risk scoring: Flag and route higher-risk use cases for review.
How it works:
- Register: Every model and agent registers with the governance layer.
- Enforce: Policy applies automatically to every call.
- Report: Give risk and legal a live view, not a quarterly audit.
Typical outcomes:
- 1 policy layer across every model and agent
- 100% AI usage visible to risk and legal
- 0 shadow AI outside the perimeter

chunks.title: AI Healthcare
chunks.text:

Purpose-built retrieval and agent tooling for payer, provider and life-sciences data, with PHI-aware masking, consent enforcement and clinical terminology built into the governance layer.
Key capabilities:
- PHI-aware by default: Automatic detection and masking of protected health information.
- Clinical terminology: ICD-10, CPT and HL7/FHIR-aware retrieval and mapping.
- Consent-enforced: Patient consent status gates every retrieval.
- Audit for regulators: HIPAA-ready logs for every access and answer.
How it works:
- Map: Classify clinical and claims data across source systems.
- Govern: Apply PHI masking and consent policy automatically.
- Activate: Build copilots for care teams, ops and research.
Typical outcomes:
- 100% PHI-aware retrieval and masking
- 0 consent violations by design
- weeks not years, to a compliant clinical copilot

chunks.title: Data Preservation
chunks.text:
Data Preservation (Cloud Archive Products). Immutable, searchable records for every era.
A governed Preservation Zone that keeps records from every system and every decade immutable, retrievable and defensible, whether the reason is regulation, litigation or institutional memory.
Key capabilities:
- WORM-capable storage: Write-once, read-many preservation with retention locks.
- Full-text and structured search: Find any record without restoring a backup.
- Legal hold: Suspend deletion instantly across affected records.
- Defensible deletion: Delete only what policy allows, with a full audit trail.
How it works:
- Classify: Apply retention schedules by record type and jurisdiction.
- Preserve: Move eligible records into the Preservation Zone.
- Prove: Produce evidence of compliant handling on demand.
Typical outcomes:
- PB scale in production today
- 100% audit-ready retention
- 0 records lost to format obsolescence

chunks.title: Oracle / OEBS Archiving
chunks.text:

chunks.title: Mainframe Archiving
chunks.text:

Key capabilities:

- MIPS reduction: Move cold data off the mainframe to cut processing cost.
- Business-readable output: Copybook-aware conversion, not raw hex dumps.
- Full-text search: Query decades of mainframe history without JCL.

- Extract: Pull data and copybook definitions from the mainframe.
- Transform: Convert to business-readable, searchable formats.
- Retire: Decommission mainframe storage on your schedule.
Typical outcomes:

- 100% history preserved and searchable
- 0 JCL required to access archived data

chunks.title: Email Archiving
chunks.text:

Capture, retain and search email and messaging across the enterprise with defensible retention, legal hold and eDiscovery-ready export, without asking users to manage their own inbox size.
Key capabilities:
- Journaling capture: Every message captured at the source, tamper-proof.
- Retention by policy: Rules by role, department or regulation.
- Legal hold in seconds: Hold a custodian's mailbox instantly, enterprise-wide.
- eDiscovery export: Standard load-file export for review platforms.
How it works:
- Capture: Journal messages from Exchange, Google Workspace or both.
- Retain: Apply retention and legal hold automatically.
- Search: Full-text search across every mailbox, live or archived.
Typical outcomes:
- 100% of mailboxes covered by policy
- mins not days, to apply a legal hold
- 0 unmanaged mailbox growth

chunks.title: File Archiving
chunks.text:
File Archiving (Cloud Archive Products). Tier cold files off primary storage, keep them one click away.
Identify and move inactive files from file shares, NAS and cloud drives to low-cost archive storage with stub-based access, so users and applications never notice the difference.
Key capabilities:
- Transparent stubbing: Files open normally; retrieval is automatic and invisible.
- Policy-based tiering: Age, size and access-pattern rules decide what moves.
- Any source: Windows and Linux file shares, NAS and cloud drives.
- Storage cost visibility: See savings by share, department or business unit.
How it works:
- Scan: Profile file shares for cold, duplicate and orphaned data.
- Archive: Move eligible files with stubs left in place.
- Reclaim: Free primary storage and defer expensive upgrades.
Typical outcomes:
- 60% less primary file storage, typical
- 0 user-visible change in file access
- $ storage upgrades deferred or avoided

chunks.title: Database Archiving
chunks.text:
Database Archiving (Cloud Archive Products). Archive inactive rows. Keep every relationship intact.
Move aged records out of production databases at the row level, preserving referential integrity across related tables so applications, reports and queries keep working exactly as before.
Key capabilities:
- Referential integrity: Related rows across tables move and stay linked together.
- Any major database: Oracle, SQL Server, DB2, PostgreSQL and more.
- Application-transparent: Archived rows remain queryable through existing apps.
- Growth control: Keep production databases at a predictable, stable size.
How it works:
- Model: Map table relationships and define archive eligibility.
- Archive: Move rows in referentially consistent batches.
- Query: Access archived and live rows through the same interface.
Typical outcomes:
- 65% smaller production database, typical
- 3x faster backup and recovery cycles
- 0 broken foreign-key relationships

chunks.title: Active Archiving for Compliance
chunks.text:

chunks.title: How to Build an Enterprise Archive in the Cloud
chunks.text:
How to Build an Enterprise Archive in the Cloud (whitepaper, gated download). A reference architecture for compliant, low-cost archiving with SOLIXCloud and the Common Data Platform.
Most cloud migrations move everything and pay for it twice. This reference architecture shows how to land inactive data in a governed, low-cost archive first, then migrate only what production really needs.
Related products: Enterprise Archiving, Common Data Platform

chunks.title: How to Build an Enterprise Archive in the Cloud: Why archives belong in the cloud now
chunks.text:
From "How to Build an Enterprise Archive in the Cloud", section "Why archives belong in the cloud now":
Ten years ago the case for an on-premises archive was storage cost. Today the case for a cloud archive is everything else: elastic ingest, object storage that is cheaper than tape, immutable retention as a native feature, and the ability to put AI to work on records the moment they land. The economics flipped; most architectures have not.
The organizations getting this right treat the archive as the first system to move, not the last. An archive-first program shrinks the production estate before it migrates, so the migration itself is smaller, faster and safer.
- 60-80% of ERP data typically inactive
- 50% smaller migrations after archive-first
- PB scale on object storage

chunks.title: How to Build an Enterprise Archive in the Cloud: Reference architecture
chunks.text:
From "How to Build an Enterprise Archive in the Cloud", section "Reference architecture":
The Solix Common Data Platform (CDP) provides four zones. The Landing zone ingests from 150+ connectors with validation and reconciliation. The Curated zone applies schema, classification and business context. The Preservation zone holds records under retention, legal hold and WORM controls. The Published zone exposes governed data products to search, SQL, REST and vector consumers.
- Object storage (S3, ADLS, GCS) as the durable substrate, Parquet/Iceberg as the open format
- Elastic compute for ingest and query, scaled independently
- A single catalog spanning archive, lake and live applications
- Policy engine for retention, hold, masking and defensible deletion
- Audit log of every access and policy decision

chunks.title: How to Build an Enterprise Archive in the Cloud: Ingest patterns that survive contact with reality
chunks.text:
From "How to Build an Enterprise Archive in the Cloud", section "Ingest patterns that survive contact with reality":
Bulk historical loads and incremental deltas need different plumbing. Bulk loads prioritize throughput and reconciliation reports; incremental loads prioritize CDC fidelity and schema evolution. CDP handles both, but the design decision that matters most is where you draw the archive boundary: by date, by business status (closed fiscal year, completed order) or by regulatory class.
The most common failure mode is archiving by date alone. Closed-status rules keep referential integrity intact and make user access seamless because users see complete business objects, not truncated ones.

chunks.title: How to Build an Enterprise Archive in the Cloud: Compliance built in, not bolted on
chunks.text:
From "How to Build an Enterprise Archive in the Cloud", section "Compliance built in, not bolted on":
SEC 17a-4, FINRA 4511, HIPAA and GDPR all reward the same design: immutable storage, retention by record class, legal hold that spans systems, and an audit trail nobody can edit. The Preservation zone implements each as configuration, with regulator-ready evidence exports.

chunks.title: How to Build an Enterprise Archive in the Cloud: Cost model
chunks.text:
From "How to Build an Enterprise Archive in the Cloud", section "Cost model":
A typical program moves inactive data from tier-1 database storage (often $5-15/GB/year fully loaded) to object storage with lifecycle tiers (under $0.30/GB/year). Add avoided license growth, faster batch windows and smaller DR footprints, and archive-first programs usually pay back within the first year.
"Our S/4HANA migration was half the size it would have been. Archive-first paid for itself before cut-over." - VP, Enterprise Applications, global manufacturer

chunks.title: Why Archive-First Is the Fastest Path to S/4HANA
chunks.text:
Why Archive-First Is the Fastest Path to S/4HANA (blog). Migrate less, cut risk and land on time by moving inactive ERP history before you move the system.
S/4HANA programs slip for one reason more than any other: they try to move two decades of history along with the system. Move the history first, and the migration gets smaller, cheaper and safer.
Related products: SAP Archiving, Enterprise Archiving

chunks.title: Why Archive-First Is the Fastest Path to S/4HANA: The hidden variable in every S/4 plan
chunks.text:
From "Why Archive-First Is the Fastest Path to S/4HANA", section "The hidden variable in every S/4 plan":
Ask a program manager what determines S/4HANA migration duration and you will hear about custom code remediation, testing cycles and business readiness. Ask a database administrator and you will hear a single number: how many terabytes we have to move. In most ECC estates, 60 to 80 percent of that volume is closed, inactive history nobody reads but everybody must keep.
Archive-first attacks the variable directly. Inactive documents, closed fiscal years and completed orders move to a governed archive before the conversion begins. What migrates is the live business. What remains accessible is everything.

chunks.title: Why Archive-First Is the Fastest Path to S/4HANA: What changes when the database is half the size
chunks.text:
From "Why Archive-First Is the Fastest Path to S/4HANA", section "What changes when the database is half the size":
- Conversion runtime drops, often from days to hours, so downtime windows become realistic
- Test cycles complete faster and cover more scenarios
- HANA memory sizing (and license) shrinks in proportion
- DR, backup and refresh footprints follow the production reduction
- Risk concentrates on live data, where the business is paying attention
- 50% smaller conversion volume, typical
- 3x faster test refresh cycles
- 1 click from archived history for users

chunks.title: Why Archive-First Is the Fastest Path to S/4HANA: But users still need the history
chunks.text:
From "Why Archive-First Is the Fastest Path to S/4HANA", section "But users still need the history":
This is where many archive programs stalled in the past: archived data disappeared into a vault nobody could query. The Solix Common Data Platform keeps archived SAP data in open formats with full business context, including attachments and relationships, and exposes it through familiar transactions, reports and search. Auditors, controllers and customer service teams see complete records without touching production.
Because the archive is a governed Preservation Zone, retention, legal hold and defensible deletion come along for free. Many programs discover their first fully documented retention schedule as a side effect.

- Retire: Decommission the legacy ECC landscape and reclaim licenses.
"We stopped treating the archive as a phase-two nicety and made it phase zero. That decision saved the go-live date." - Program Director, S/4HANA transformation

chunks.title: The Trust Perimeter: A New Model for Business-Led AI
chunks.text:
The Trust Perimeter: A New Model for Business-Led AI (blog). Why IT should define boundaries, not build every solution, and how Enterprise Edition makes it real.
Central IT cannot build every AI solution the business wants, and the business cannot be trusted to build them without guardrails. The trust perimeter resolves the tension: IT defines the boundary, the business builds inside it.
Related products: Solix Enterprise Edition, Enterprise AI

chunks.title: The Trust Perimeter: A New Model for Business-Led AI: Two failure modes
chunks.text:
From "The Trust Perimeter: A New Model for Business-Led AI", section "Two failure modes":
The first failure mode is the bottleneck: every copilot, dashboard and agent waits in a central backlog while the business builds workarounds in spreadsheets and unsanctioned tools. The second is the free-for-all: teams spin up their own models on their own exports and nobody can answer where the data went.
Both are governance failures dressed as delivery problems. The fix is not more control or less; it is control in the right place.

chunks.title: The Trust Perimeter: A New Model for Business-Led AI: What a trust perimeter is
chunks.text:
From "The Trust Perimeter: A New Model for Business-Led AI", section "What a trust perimeter is":
A trust perimeter is the set of policies, data products and tools inside which business builders can create solutions without asking permission, because permission is already encoded. IT decides which data is published, how it is classified and masked, what models are approved, what budgets apply and how every action is audited. Everything inside that boundary is safe by construction.
- Curated data products with semantic context and lineage
- Access, masking and retention enforced at query time
- Approved model catalog with per-team budgets
- Evaluation and monitoring as platform services
- A full audit trail of prompts, retrievals and answers
IT moves from building solutions to building the perimeter. The business moves from waiting to shipping. Governance moves from a review gate to a property of the platform.

- 1 perimeter instead of fifty exceptions
- 0 shadow data copies

chunks.title: The Trust Perimeter: A New Model for Business-Led AI: Start with one boundary
chunks.text:

You do not need a complete perimeter to begin. Pick one domain, publish three data products, approve one model, set a budget and let one team build. Measure time to value and policy exceptions. Then expand the boundary.

chunks.title: Consumer Data Privacy Automation Playbook: The scale problem
chunks.text:
From "Consumer Data Privacy Automation Playbook", section "The scale problem":
A single data subject access request can touch thirty systems. A right-to-be-forgotten request must find and delete personal data everywhere it lives, while respecting legal exceptions. At volume, manual fulfilment is not slow; it is impossible.
- 30+ systems per typical DSAR
- 95% of requests automatable
- 2 hrs fulfilment time after automation

chunks.title: Consumer Data Privacy Automation Playbook: Operating model
chunks.text:
From "Consumer Data Privacy Automation Playbook", section "Operating model":
Successful programs pair a privacy office that owns policy with a data platform team that owns execution. Solix Consumer Data Privacy sits between them: policy templates translate regulations into executable rules, and the Common Data Platform executes them across structured, unstructured, live and archived data.
- Discovery: ML classification of personal data across every source, refreshed continuously
- Intake: verified request capture with identity checks and jurisdiction routing
- Fulfilment: orchestrated search, redaction, export or deletion with legal exception handling
- Evidence: immutable audit packs per request and per regulation

chunks.title: Consumer Data Privacy Automation Playbook: Reference workflows
chunks.text:
From "Consumer Data Privacy Automation Playbook", section "Reference workflows":
- DSAR: Intake, verify, discover, compile, redact, deliver, evidence. Target: under 4 hours.
- Erasure: Discover, evaluate exceptions, delete or anonymize, confirm, evidence.
- Consent: Capture purpose-based consent, enforce at query time, report on coverage.
- Retention: Apply minimization schedules to live and archived data with defensible deletion.
Time to fulfil, percentage automated, exceptions per hundred requests, and evidence completeness. Track them monthly and publish them to the board.

chunks.title: Consumer Data Privacy Automation Playbook: Archived data is personal data too
chunks.text:
From "Consumer Data Privacy Automation Playbook", section "Archived data is personal data too":
Regulators do not exempt backups, archives or retired systems. Because Solix privacy workflows run on the same platform that preserves that data, a single request reaches every era of the estate.

chunks.title: The Buyer's Guide to Enterprise AI Governance
chunks.text:
The Buyer's Guide to Enterprise AI Governance (ebook, gated download). Twelve questions to ask any AI vendor before your data touches their model.
Twelve questions worth asking any AI vendor before your enterprise data touches their model, drawn from customer procurement conversations we've sat through.
Related products: AI Governance, Enterprise AI

chunks.title: The Buyer's Guide to Enterprise AI Governance: Why this guide exists
chunks.text:
From "The Buyer's Guide to Enterprise AI Governance", section "Why this guide exists":
Most enterprise AI procurement processes ask about model quality and pricing, and stop there. The questions that actually determine whether a program survives its first security review are about data: where it goes, who can see it, and what happens when something goes wrong. This guide collects the twelve questions we see customers wish they'd asked earlier.

chunks.title: The Buyer's Guide to Enterprise AI Governance: Access and retrieval
chunks.text:
From "The Buyer's Guide to Enterprise AI Governance", section "Access and retrieval":
- Does retrieval respect the asker's existing access permissions, or a separate, broader index?
- Can you prove, per query, which access policy applied?
- What happens to a query against data the asker isn't authorized to see?

chunks.title: The Buyer's Guide to Enterprise AI Governance: Data handling
chunks.text:
From "The Buyer's Guide to Enterprise AI Governance", section "Data handling":
- Is data copied into a separate vector store, and if so, who governs it?
- How is personal and sensitive data masked before it reaches the model?
- What is the retention policy for prompts and responses?
The single most common shadow-AI failure we see: a well-meaning team exports a "read-only" data extract into a third-party tool for embedding, and that extract quietly becomes a permanent, ungoverned copy.

chunks.title: The Buyer's Guide to Enterprise AI Governance: Governance and audit
chunks.text:
From "The Buyer's Guide to Enterprise AI Governance", section "Governance and audit":
- Can every AI answer be traced back to its source records?
- Is there a model inventory: which models touch which data, everywhere?
- How would you answer a regulator asking what an AI system did with a specific customer's data?

chunks.title: The Buyer's Guide to Enterprise AI Governance: Operations
chunks.text:
From "The Buyer's Guide to Enterprise AI Governance", section "Operations":
- What is the cost and quota model per team or use case?
- How do you detect and respond to model drift or quality regression?
- What is the actual time from a scoped use case to a production copilot?
"We stopped evaluating AI vendors on model benchmarks and started evaluating them on their answer to 'where does our data go.' It changed the shortlist completely." - CISO, regulated financial services firm

chunks.title: Twenty Years of Enterprise Data: Five Lessons
chunks.text:
Twenty Years of Enterprise Data: Five Lessons (leadership). Our founder on what changed, what didn't, and what he'd tell a CDO starting today.
Solix founder Sai Gundavelli on what changed in two decades of enterprise data management, what didn't, and what he'd tell a CDO starting today.

chunks.title: Twenty Years of Enterprise Data: Five Lessons: 1. The data doesn't get younger
chunks.text:
From "Twenty Years of Enterprise Data: Five Lessons", section "1. The data doesn't get younger":
Every enterprise I've worked with has data from a system nobody remembers approving. The instinct is to treat it as a cleanup problem. It isn't. It's a stewardship problem, and it never ends, because the newest system today is next decade's legacy system.

chunks.title: Twenty Years of Enterprise Data: Five Lessons: 2. Governance that slows people down gets routed around
chunks.text:
From "Twenty Years of Enterprise Data: Five Lessons", section "2. Governance that slows people down gets routed around":
The archives and catalogs that actually get used are the ones that are faster than the alternative, not just more compliant than it. If the governed path is slower than a shadow spreadsheet, people will build the spreadsheet. Every product decision we make starts from that constraint.

chunks.title: Twenty Years of Enterprise Data: Five Lessons: 3. AI didn't change the fundamentals, it raised the stakes
chunks.text:
From "Twenty Years of Enterprise Data: Five Lessons", section "3. AI didn't change the fundamentals, it raised the stakes":
Bad data governance used to cost you a failed audit. Now it can cost you a model that confidently tells a customer something false, sourced from data it should never have touched. The fundamentals - know what you have, control who sees it, prove what happened - matter more, not less.
- 20+ years in enterprise data
- 1000s of systems retired for customers
- 0 shortcuts we'd take again

chunks.title: Twenty Years of Enterprise Data: Five Lessons: 4. Retirement is a bigger lever than anyone budgets for
chunks.text:
From "Twenty Years of Enterprise Data: Five Lessons", section "4. Retirement is a bigger lever than anyone budgets for":
Nobody puts "decommission the old system" at the top of a transformation roadmap. It should be closer to the top. The applications quietly costing the most, in license fees, specialist staff and audit risk, are usually the ones everyone has stopped thinking about.

chunks.title: Twenty Years of Enterprise Data: Five Lessons: 5. The best programs treat data as a product, not a byproduct
chunks.text:
From "Twenty Years of Enterprise Data: Five Lessons", section "5. The best programs treat data as a product, not a byproduct":
The organizations getting the most from their data long ago stopped asking IT to "just give us access" and started asking for governed, documented, trustworthy data products, the same way they'd ask for any other internal product. That shift in posture matters more than any single tool.
Start with an honest inventory of what you actually have, across every era. You cannot govern, secure or activate what you haven't found.
